name: Caointeach

attributes.attribute: a Highland name for the banshee
a spirit that wailed by a waterfall
wept loudly before a great disaster
mourned for days before the Glencoe massacre
washed the clothes of the doomed at night
was kind and wept with human grief
a spirit that washed clothes to warn of death

sources: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
text:
Caointeach is a Scottish Highland spirit.
Highlanders also call her Caoineag.
The names mean wailer and weeper.
She is one kind of banshee.
She wailed ahead of a death so people would know.
She sat by a waterfall and wept before a death.
A big disaster drew a loud cry from her.
The Caointeach of the Macdonalds mourned for days before the Glencoe massacre.
At night she washed the clothes of the doomed, like the Washer at the Ford.
She had no ill will.
Grief touched her and made her cry more.
Yet people did not greet her.
The rule was to give no reward.
A gift could drive her off and end the warning.
The Welsh form of her has its own name.
She is the Cyhyreath.
Her voice sounds like the groans of a dying person.

okr.objective: Caointeach is a Highland spirit whose cry tells of a death to come.
key_results: Caointeach is the Highland name for the banshee, that is the wailer.
Her cry rose before a death.
She mourned the Macdonalds before the Glencoe massacre.
She washed the clothes of the doomed at night.
The Welsh call their own kind of her the Cyhyreath.
okr.evidence: Monaghan, Patricia. The Encyclopedia of Celtic Mythology and Folklore. Checkmark Books, 2008.
